settings.windowProbe.label: GNOME Screen Helper
settings.windowProbe.hint: GNOME Wayland does not tell ordinary apps where each window is, so window quick-pick needs help. Clippy ships a small shell extension that supplies window geometry, to Clippy only. Screenshots do not depend on it — they come straight from the compositor.
settings.windowProbe.detailUnsupported: Screenshots and window quick-pick already work here without an extra service.
settings.windowProbe.detailActive: Screenshots and window quick-pick both go through the helper.
settings.windowProbe.detailBlocked: The service is installed, but GNOME extensions are turned off system-wide. Enable extensions in GNOME Tweaks or the Extensions app.
settings.windowProbe.detailPendingUpdate: A newer helper was written to disk. Log out and back in once so GNOME loads it. Nothing is broken meanwhile: window quick-pick and screenshots both keep working.
settings.windowProbe.detailPendingLogout: The service is installed. GNOME loads new extensions only at login, so log out once (or reboot) to activate it.
settings.windowProbe.detailMissing: On GNOME Wayland the screenshot shortcut may fail without it, and the window under the cursor is never highlighted.
settings.windowProbe.installedNeedsLogou: Service installed. Log out once to activate it.
settings.captureDiagnostics.label: Screenshot Diagnostics
settings.captureDiagnostics.hint: If the screenshot overlay is offset, oversized, or spills onto another monitor, this collects the numbers needed to explain why: what each monitor reports, how big the captured stage image is, and the result of every geometry self-check. It contains no image pixels and no window titles, is saved only on this machine, and is never uploaded.
settings.captureDiagnostics.notePlacehol: e.g. laptop screen offset up-left after plugging in an external monitor
settings.captureDiagnostics.noteHint: Goes into the report to describe your monitor layout and the symptom. Optional.
settings.captureDiagnostics.copied: Report copied. Paste it into the issue.
capture.windowProbeHint: Screenshots work better with a small GNOME service: install it in Settings → Screenshot, then log out once. Drag to select an area in the meantime.
